name: benefit_params
description: The tunables the statutory weekly indemnity benefit is computed from (Story 3.1, AD-8). A document of its own for intake_required_documents' and injury_capture's reason: services/financials owns the benefit formula, while derivation_thresholds is the single argument every REGISTERED DERIVATION is built from — folding a service's parameters into it would make the registry's contract mean 'whatever anybody needed a number for'. The one benefit parameter that is NOT here is ptdSeverityThreshold, and its absence is the same argument in the other direction: which indemnity type a claim is on is a registered derivation (AD-10), so its cut-off lives in derivation_thresholds v4 and this document never restates it. compute_benefit asks the derivation whether the claim is PTD and pays the rate below accordingly; the threshold therefore has exactly one reader. RATES ARE BASIS POINTS, not percentages: 6667 is 66.67%. The unit is the one claim.comp_rate_override_bp stores, so a handler's override and the default it replaces are the same kind of integer and the whole calculation is integer arithmetic — 66.67 has no exact binary representation, and a default expressed as a float beside an override expressed as an integer would make 'is this claim overridden?' a comparison two values can fail by 1e-14. (The money convention's 'integer cents across the ZEN boundary' does not literally apply — a comp rate is a rate, not money — but its reason does.) defaultCompRateBp is the statutory two-thirds every US jurisdiction in this portfolio pays a temporarily disabled worker; ptdCompRateBp is the full wage a permanent total disability is paid at. waitingPeriodDays is the statutory wait before the first indemnity payment; Story 3.1 only DISPLAYS it in the payment-schedule note, and Story 3.3 is where the schedule that applies it (first payment = DOI + waitingPeriodDays) is generated — which is precisely why it is data now rather than a literal in 3.3's generator. All three are the prototype's values (computeBenefit lines 715-728), ported exactly.
